loss_spans: Harness._on_escalation_resolved calls event.set() on _escalation_events[task_id] for EVERY resolution, close_only and dismiss=True included, before it dispatches the action, so any closure wakes a live workflow waiting on that task id.

Also, queue.submit_resolved leaves resolution_action None, and the legacy D10 mapping reads a resolved record as 'resume' (re-pend). Stamp esc.resolution_action='close_only' before submit_resolved when you mean a no-effect closure.
To suppress the wake as well, you need an explicit early return at the top of the callback, like the eval-lane guard keyed on shared.eval_lane.eval_lane_provenance.
